consensus: The pair is built as a WHEEL/DISCARD deck with Brallin's ping as the clock and a Curiosity-class enchantment on Brallin as the kill: EDHREC's 3,924 decks tag Wheels 488, Discard 277, Cycling 147, +1/+1 Counters 134, Combo 93, Voltron 42, Humans 9. The consensus 99 is 35 lands with a cycling-land package, six to nine two-mana rocks, four to six big wheels, ten-plus one- and two-mana loot/rummage spells, five to seven discard/draw payoff creatures, nine interaction slots and the two boots; Curiosity (59%), Faithless Looting (73%), Windfall (72%), Frantic Search (67%) and Swords to Plowshares (63%) are the spine. 'Flying Humans' is not built by anyone at scale; the flying plan in practice is Shabraz plus Shark Typhoon plus the two Shark creatures. This list agrees with consensus on the wheel and draw-payoff core and disagrees on everything the builder filled: no Curiosity effect, two loots against fifteen wheels, four interaction pieces, zero cycling lands, Treasure ramp in place of Signets, and eighteen builder-chosen spells that appear in fewer than 13% of lists each.

findings.claim: THE KILL IS A CURIOSITY-CLASS ENCHANTMENT ON BRALLIN, AND THIS LIST RUNS NONE OF THE THREE. Curiosity is in 2317/3924 (59%) of pair decks, Ophidian Eye 1239/3924 (32%), Tandem Lookout 1122/3924 (29%); on the combo-tagged page Curiosity is 82/93 (88%). Commander Spellbook's Brallin + Curiosity page: prerequisites 'Curiosity attached to Brallin' and 'Hand size exceeds maximum'; steps 'During your cleanup step, discard to your maximum hand size' -> 'Brallin triggers for each card discarded' -> 'Curiosity triggers, causing you to draw a card for each damage dealt' -> 'Pass priority, moving to an additional cleanup step' -> repeat; labelled 'Spicy (Bracket 3-4+)', 5,089 decks. Tandem Lookout (1,995 decks) and Ophidian Eye (2,232) are the same loop. Short of the loop, the same enchantment turns every wheel's 7 pings into 7 draws and 7 Shabraz counters. BENCH NOTE: the deck already holds Niv-Mizzet, Parun and Glint-Horn Buccaneer, so any ONE of these three adds THREE two-card infinites that `combo_details.json` already indexes (ids 17/219/1050 for Curiosity, 47/550/2192 for Ophidian Eye, 58/513/2342 for Tandem Lookout) — `deck-facts` would go from 0 contained combos to 3, which is the standard-v3 pod's own exclusion rule. Whether that is acceptable for the SUBJECT at a bracket-3 table is the pilot's call, not recon's.

THE CONSENSUS RUNS CHEAP LOOT/RUMMAGE, NOT FIFTEEN WHEELS. The four cards above 65% inclusion are Faithless Looting 2864/3924 (73%), Windfall 2817/3924 (72%), Frantic Search 2632/3924 (67%) and Swords; Thrill of Possibility 1732/3924 (44%), Change of Fortune 1668/3924 (43%), Brainstorm 1653/3924 (42%), Faithful Mending 1581/3924 (40%), Heartwarming Redemption 1519/3924 (39%), Cathartic Reunion 1507/3924 (38%), Izzet Charm 1388/3924 (35%), Fateful Showdown 1078/3924 (27%), Careful Study 1063/3924 (27%), Decaying Time Loop 936/3924 (24%) all outrank the big wheels: Reforge the Soul 1014/3924 (26%), Wheel of Misfortune 947/3924 (24%), Wheel of Fortune 778/3924 (20%), Burning Inquiry 721/3924 (18%), Echo of Eons 115/488 (24%) of wheels-tagged decks, Winds of Change 84/488 (17%), Molten Psyche 37/488 (8%), Khorvath's Fury 27/488 (6%), Whirlpool Warrior 42/488 (9%), Commit // Memory 43/488 (9%); Time Reversal is below the listing cut on the 3,924-deck page. mtg-agents (2026-08-27): 'Six to nine wheels, ten to fourteen payoffs, and at least three ways to protect the payoff that matters' and 'The mistake I see most often is a deck with twelve wheels and four payoffs. That deck draws a lot of cards and loses.' The current core declares fifteen wheel effects and two loots (Faithless Looting, Tolarian Winds). The average deck's shape is 15 instants / 10 sorceries: one-mana instant-speed discard that triggers Brallin on the opponent's turn.

INTERACTION IS THE BIGGEST HOLE AGAINST THE AVERAGE LIST. The average deck carries Swords to Plowshares 2467/3924 (63%), Path to Exile 1904/3924 (49%), Counterspell 1779/3924 (45%), Dovin's Veto 1231/3924 (31%), Arcane Denial 1190/3924 (30%), Blasphemous Act 1136/3924 (29%), An Offer You Can't Refuse 942/3924 (24%), plus Negate / Generous Gift / Chaos Warp / Deflecting Swat in the wheels-tagged page (96-127 of 488 each) — roughly nine interaction slots. `deck-facts` counts this list at 2 counterspells, 1 spot removal and 1 sweeper (Elesh Norn). mtg-agents: opponents 'receive fresh cards through wheels', so run 'fast, cheap interaction'; commanderdeckmaker: 'Nekusar decks become immediate targets.' Swords and Path carry NEGATIVE synergy on every EDHREC page (they are generic), which is the point — they are there because the archetype needs answers, not because they wheel.

THE MANA BASE PEOPLE RUN IS 35 LANDS WITH A CYCLING-LAND PACKAGE AND SIX TO EIGHT TWO-MANA ROCKS, NOT 36 UNTAPPED DUALS WITH TREASURE ARTIFACTS. Average deck: 35 lands (23 nonbasic incl. Lonely Sandbar, Forgotten Cave, Secluded Steppe, Ash Barrens, Irrigated Farmland; 15 basics) and 11 artifacts, of which 9 are rocks. Cycling lands: Lonely Sandbar 1511/3924 (39%), Forgotten Cave 1486/3924 (38%), Secluded Steppe 1383/3924 (35%), Irrigated Farmland 1297/3924 (33%), Ash Barrens 1264/3924 (32%), Remote Isle 923/3924 (24%), Smoldering Crater 896/3924 (23%), Drifting Meadow 882/3924 (22%); on the cycling page they are the top-synergy cards outright (Forgotten Cave 0.686). Rocks: Talisman of Creativity 1889/3924 (48%), Izzet Signet 1862/3924 (47%), Azorius Signet 1737/3924 (44%), Talisman of Progress 1598/3924 (41%), Talisman of Conviction 1519/3924 (39%), Boros Signet 1510/3924 (38%), Fellwar Stone 1351/3924 (34%), Thought Vessel 1103/3924 (28%). Utility: Reliquary Tower 1746/3924 (44%) (in), Desolate Lighthouse 839/3924 (21%), Geier Reach Sanitarium 776/3924 (20%), Cephalid Coliseum 79/488 (16%). The builder's twelve land picks are all below EDHREC's listing cut on the 3,924-deck page (City of Brass and Mana Confluence sit at 65 and 61 of 488 wheels decks; Skycloud Expanse 67/488 and is the 25th-most-cut card from the precon). This list has zero cycling lands and two rocks; its ramp slots are Treasure pieces (Sticky Fingers, Generous Plunderer, Treasure Map, Currency Converter, Artist's Talent, Sorcerer Class) that appear in 0-12% of lists.

DISCARD-SIDE PAYOFFS BEYOND THE COMMANDER: the lists run five to seven, this one runs Glint-Horn Buccaneer and Containment Construct. Captain Howler, Sea Scourge 1781/3487 (51%), Marauding Mako 1679/3487 (48%) (both Sharks, both post-date many lists so potential is lower), Ghostly Pilferer 1568/3924 (40%), Magmakin Artillerist 1525/3444 (44%), Surly Badgersaur 1480/3924 (38%), Forgotten Creation 1370/3924 (35%), Tandem Lookout 1122/3924 (29%), Niv-Mizzet, the Firemind 1120/3924 (29%), Ledger Shredder 1107/3924 (28%), Esper Sentinel 1030/3924 (26%). Brallin's solo page puts Glint-Horn at 82/94 and Surly Badgersaur at 64/94. SCG (Bennie Smith, 2020-04-13) called Surly Badgersaur 'a cute red spin on Bone Miser'. The builder-chosen creatures — Jaxis, Marketback Walker, Mindless Automaton, Vanguard Suppressor, Silent Hallcreeper, Stromkirk Noble, Goblin Engineer, Elesh Norn — are all below the listing cut on the 3,924-deck page.

DRAW-DOUBLERS AND HAND ENGINES THE LISTS RUN THAT THIS ONE DOES NOT: Teferi's Ageless Insight 1766/3924 (45%) (0.394 synergy; 142/262 of solo-Shabraz decks), Monument to Endurance 1317/3459 (38%), Bag of Holding 881/3924 (22%), Mystic Remora 873/3924 (22%), Whirlwind of Thought 845/3924 (22%), Tectonic Reformation 765/3924 (19%), Fluctuator 672/3924 (17%) (81/147 on the cycling page; SCG: 'a critical mana reducer for repeated cycling'), Alhammarret's Archive 639/3924 (16%), Wizard Class 638/3924 (16%). Of this list's engines, Psychosis Crawler 1729/3924 (44%), The Locust God 1726/3924 (44%), Ominous Seas 1847/3924 (47%), Shark Typhoon 1632/3924 (42%), Jace's Archivist 1400/3924 (36%), Niv-Mizzet, Parun 1361/3924 (35%), Chasm Skulker 1097/3924 (28%) agree with consensus; Mind's Eye, Kefnet the Mindful, Enduring Curiosity, Improbable Alliance, Irencrag Pyromancer, Arjun and Decree of Silence are all below the listing cut.

PROTECTION FOR TWO COMMANDERS: the boots are consensus and already in (Swiftfoot Boots 1375/3924 (35%), Lightning Greaves 1091/3924 (28%)); beyond them the lists reach for free or instant-speed spells, not more equipment: Fierce Guardianship 886/3924 (23%) (a Game Changer), Deflecting Swat 127/488 (26%), Boros Charm 99/488 (20%), Teferi's Protection 74/488 (15%), Grand Abolisher 95/488 (19%), Silence 66/488 (14%). mtg-agents: 'A wheel deck that cannot keep a Psychosis Crawler alive for one rotation is just an expensive group hug deck.' The cEDH average (29 decks) runs Grand Abolisher, Silence, Deflecting Swat and Fierce Guardianship together.

'FLYING HUMANS' IS A FOOTNOTE, NOT A PLAN. Nine of 3,924 pair decks carry the Humans tag, and the humans-theme page's own high-synergy cards are Sharks — Thunderhead Gunner, Captain Howler, Marauding Mako, Shark Typhoon, Loan Shark — i.e. even those nine are shark decks. Shabraz's solo page (262 decks) tags Wheels 26 / +1/+1 Counters 13 / Card Draw 11 / Flying 8 / Humans 1; the one Archidekt solo 'flying' list fetched (HapaKuya, 2025-11-01) is flying-tribal anthems (Kangee, Empyrean Eagle, Steel-Plume Marshal) with no Human package. Draftsim (2025-08-21) treats the activated abilities as 'combat utility'. What the flying plan actually looks like in practice is Shabraz plus Shark Typhoon's X/X flyers plus the two Shark creatures; no fetched list builds the Human side.

SELF-DECKING LINES AND THE LAB-MAN QUESTION. Laboratory Maniac is in 613/3924 (16%) of pair decks (98/488 wheels-tagged; 100/262 solo-Shabraz), Jace, Wielder of Mysteries 312/3924 (8%); Thassa's Oracle and Drogskol Reaver are both below the listing cut on the pair page even though Drogskol Reaver is 94/262 in solo-Shabraz lists. Spellbook: Shabraz + Drogskol Reaver draws the deck (6,466 decks, 'Spicy (Bracket 3-4+)') and 'In response to the final Shabraz trigger, remove a combo piece or win the game to avoid losing by drawing from an empty library'; Shabraz + Marina Vendrell's Grimoire is 'Ruthless (Bracket 4+)' and 'will result in you eventually drawing from an empty library'. The cEDH average (29 decks) wins through Underworld Breach + Brain Freeze + Lion's Eye Diamond and Curiosity, with no Oracle at all. Reading: a Lab-Man line is a bracket-4 posture here, and the draw loops that feed it need instant-speed removal of their own piece.

DAMAGE AMPLIFIERS FOR BRALLIN'S PINGS ARE A MINORITY PLAY; EXTRA COMBATS DO NOT APPEAR AT ALL. Ojer Axonil, Deepest Might 292/3924 (7%), Torbran, Thane of Red Fell 39/488 (8%); Solphim, Mayhem Dominus and Fiery Emancipation are below the listing cut on the pair page. MTGRocks (Nathan Ball, 2026-04-26) recommends 'damage doublers' and board wipes that 'leverage their scaling bodies' (Chandra's Ignition, Soul Immolation) and names Grafted Exoskeleton and Basilisk Collar. No extra-combat card appears in any card list extracted from the EDHREC pages fetched (the section extracts are top-N, so this bounds inclusion below roughly 250 of 3,924, not at zero). For a combo-free bracket-3 build the amplifier is the combo-free way to make the ping a clock: Ojer Axonil turns each 1-damage Brallin trigger into 4 without creating an indexed line.

HAND-SIZE TRICKS: THE LISTS KEEP THE TOWER AND VESSEL AND MOSTLY SKIP THE PUZZLE BOX. Reliquary Tower 1746/3924 (44%), Thought Vessel 1103/3924 (28%), Containment Construct 1055/3924 (27%), Sevinne's Reclamation 838/3924 (21%), Alhammarret's Archive 639/3924 (16%), Teferi's Puzzle Box 320/3924 (8%), Library of Leng 33/488 (7%) of wheels-tagged decks. The precon-upgrade page shows Reliquary Tower among the CUT cards (0.183 unpopularity) — a minority cuts it, consistent with the Spellbook prerequisite for the Curiosity loop, 'Hand size exceeds maximum'. This list runs Puzzle Box, Library of Leng, Containment Construct and Reliquary Tower together; whether the no-maximum-hand-size pieces and a cleanup-step discard kill can coexist is a stack question, not a recon one.

ASYMMETRIC WHEEL PIECES AND THE SOCIAL COST. Narset, Parter of Veils 875/3924 (22%) (Game Changer), Smothering Tithe 1161/3924 (30%) (in), Rhystic Study 1216/3924 (31%) (in), Alms Collector 38/488 (8%); Notion Thief is outside Jeskai. commanderdeckmaker: 'A wheel without Nekusar or damage effects on the board is just giving everyone new hands' and 'Nekusar decks become immediate targets'; mtg-agents: 'A wheel with no payoff on the battlefield is usually a mistake in a four-player game.' The two Game Changers already in the list set the bracket floor at 3; adding Narset keeps it at 3 by count (three GCs is the bracket-3 ceiling under the Oct-2025 rules as the bench encodes them) — run `bracket-check` before assuming.

THE CYCLING SUB-ARCHETYPE (147 decks) IS A DIFFERENT DECK FROM THE WHEELS ONE (488) AND THIS LIST STRADDLES THEM. Cycling-page top cards: Fluctuator 81/147, Curator of Mysteries 78/147, Drannith Stinger 75/147, Nimble Obstructionist 71/147, Astral Drift 60/147, New Perspectives 56/147, Valiant Rescuer 60/147, Drannith Healer 58/147, Flourishing Fox 56/147, Raugrin Crystal 94/147, Countervailing Winds 66/147, Neutralize 86/147, Forsake the Worldly 64/147, Boon of the Wish-Giver 60/147, Akroma's Vengeance 53/147, Zenith Flare 52/147. On the full pair page those same cards sit at Astral Drift 435/3924 (11%), Drake Haven 427/3924 (11%), Curator 728/3924 (19%), Nimble Obstructionist 681/3924 (17%), New Perspectives 333/3924 (8%). The precon-upgrade page's most-added cards are the cycling package (Drannith Stinger 38/82, Flourishing Fox 28/82, Drannith Healer 27/82). SCG (2020) read the pair as 'a cycling-focused Commander deck rather than traditional tribal'. If the pilot keeps Astral Drift / Drake Haven / Curator / Obstructionist, the cycling lands and Fluctuator are what make them fire; if not, those four are the cut.

WHAT THE cEDH AND 'EXPENSIVE' LISTS ADD, FOR THE BRACKET LINE THIS DECK MUST NOT CROSS. cEDH average (29 decks): 29 lands + 13 fast-mana artifacts, 24 instants, wins through Underworld Breach + Brain Freeze + LED and Curiosity/Ophidian Eye/Tandem Lookout; expensive-optimized (20 decks): 31 lands, Curiosity + Ophidian Eye + Tandem Lookout + Cool but Rude, Breach, Timetwister, Jeska's Will, Gamble, Mystical/Enlightened Tutor. Underworld Breach is in 606/3924 (15%) of all pair lists and would complete three indexed three-card lines with Smothering Tithe + Wheel of Fortune / Windfall / Reforge the Soul already in the 99 (combo ids 101, 483, 4777). These name the cards a bracket-3 build deliberately omits: Breach, Jeska's Will, Gamble, the tutors, Fierce Guardianship, Cyclonic Rift, The One Ring. Recorded so the diagnosis can say why they are absent rather than treat them as gaps.

known_failure_modes: Wheeling with no payoff on the battlefield: 'A wheel without Nekusar or damage effects on the board is just giving everyone new hands' (commanderdeckmaker); 'A wheel with no payoff on the battlefield is usually a mistake in a four-player game' (mtg-agents, 2026-08-27).
Losing the payoff and becoming group hug: 'A wheel deck that cannot keep a Psychosis Crawler alive for one rotation is just an expensive group hug deck' (mtg-agents).

Becoming the table's target once the engine is visible: 'Nekusar decks become immediate targets' (commanderdeckmaker); opponents 'receive fresh cards through wheels' so cheap interaction matters (mtg-agents).
Over-wheeling relative to payoffs: 'a deck with twelve wheels and four payoffs ... draws a lot of cards and loses' (mtg-agents).

Self-decking on a draw loop: the Shabraz + Drogskol Reaver and Shabraz + Marina Vendrell's Grimoire lines end in 'drawing from an empty library' unless a piece is removed at instant speed (Commander Spellbook; MTGRocks 2026-04-26).

Kill line gated on hand size: the Brallin + Curiosity/Ophidian Eye/Tandem Lookout loops require 'Hand size exceeds maximum' at cleanup (Commander Spellbook), so no-maximum-hand-size permanents can remove the loop's trigger — unverified interaction, see gaps.

The precon's own shape is what people cut: the 82-deck precon-upgrade page's most-cut cards are the Impetus auras, Agitator Ant, Cryptic Trilobite, Ethereal Forager and Akim — the go-wide/goad half of Timeless Wisdom — and the most-added are the cycling package and Curiosity.
contested: Big wheels versus cheap loots: the brief's fifteen-wheel core is a stronger commitment than any fetched list makes; EDHREC inclusion ranks Faithless Looting / Frantic Search / Thrill of Possibility above Reforge the Soul / Wheel of Misfortune / Wheel of Fortune, and mtg-agents caps wheels at six to nine. No source argues for fifteen.

No-maximum-hand-size pieces: Reliquary Tower (44%) and Thought Vessel (28%) are consensus, but the Curiosity-class kill's stated prerequisite is a hand above maximum at cleanup, and a minority of precon-upgraders cut the Tower. The sources do not resolve this; it needs a stack scenario.

Lab-Man/Oracle lines: 38% of solo-Shabraz lists run Laboratory Maniac, 16% of pair lists do, the cEDH average runs none (it wins through Breach + Brain Freeze and Curiosity). Bracket estimate from Spellbook is 3-4+ for the Reaver line and 4+ for the Grimoire line.

Damage amplifiers: MTGRocks recommends them; EDHREC inclusion is 7% (Ojer Axonil) and below the cut for Solphim / Fiery Emancipation. A bracket-3 combo-free build has more reason to want one than the average list does.

Cycling versus wheels: the two EDHREC sub-archetypes share Glint-Horn / Windfall / Faithless Looting but diverge on lands (cycling: Desert cycle, Irrigated Farmland, Ash Barrens, Fluctuator) and creatures (cycling: Drannith Stinger, Flourishing Fox, Drannith Healer). This list carries four cycling payoffs with no cycling lands.

Curiosity at a bracket-3 table: Spellbook labels the line 'Spicy (Bracket 3-4+)'; the bench's standard-v3 pod excludes seats with any contained two-card infinite. Adding one Curiosity-class card puts three such lines in `deck-facts`. Whether the subject is held to the pod's rule is a pilot decision.

gaps: Moxfield: site, api.moxfield.com and api2.moxfield.com all returned HTTP 403 on 2026-09-10 (as on 2026-09-09). The four Moxfield cEDH primers that search surfaced ('Curious Wheels', 'The Last Shark Rider', 'Curiosity Kill', 'Bralin Combo') are unread; their search snippets describe 'Curiosity + Ghostly Pilferer' and 'LED + Brain Freeze + Underworld Breach' lines and one argues against no-maximum-hand-size slots because 'discarding to hand size every turn ... means extra damage' — recorded here as unverified, no URL cited.

TappedOut (fire-shark-tornado, brallin-and-shabraz-wheels, ?fmt=txt), MTGNexus ('The Shark and His Boy' thread), Aetherhub (brallin-wheels writeup), MTGGoldfish (deck pages and /download), mtgdecks.net: all HTTP 403. edh.fandom.com/wiki/Wheels: HTTP 402.

reddit.com is blocked for this agent's user agent on both fetch and search, so no r/EDH or r/CompetitiveEDH thread is cited; 'what people warn about' rests on two blogs and the Spellbook prerequisites rather than pilot testimony.
YouTube deck techs (e.g. the May-2020 '10 Min. DeckTech ... Wheels on the Bus are JESKAI') have no readable transcript here and are not cited.

No source is specific to a bracket-3, zero-combo table. EDHREC's bracket-3 filtered page was not fetched; Spellbook's bracket labels are its own estimates. The bracket-3 reading in findings is inference from the Spellbook labels plus the bench's pod definition, and the diagnosis should re-derive it with `bracket-check`.
No fetched primer states a wheel COUNT for this pair; the 'six to nine' figure is a generic wheel-deck ratio (mtg-agents) and the '8-12' figure (commanderdeckmaker) is Nekusar-shaped.

The interaction between no-maximum-hand-size permanents (Reliquary Tower, Thought Vessel, Library of Leng) and the Brallin + Curiosity cleanup loop is a rules question this recon does not settle — needs a stack scenario (`resolve-stack`).

EDHREC main-page cardlists are truncated top-N per section, so 'below the listing cut' means below roughly 250 of 3,924 decks, not zero; the wheels-theme page (488) gives exact counts for several of those cards and is cited where it does.
Ownership was not checked: the pilot stated it is not a constraint for this deck.
